HYP-007.title: Write schemas lack max_length matching VARCHAR columns -> DataError 500 on PostgreSQL
HYP-007.description: schemas.py fields (Category/Tag name, Post title/slug/excerpt/cover_image, Comment nickname/email) have no max_length while the models use VARCHAR(n). On SQLite over-length rows store fine (CI stays green); on PostgreSQL they raise sqlalchemy DataError, which the crud IntegrityError handlers do not catch -> 500.

EV-015.title: No max_length on 8 write fields vs VARCHAR(50/100/200/500) columns
EV-015.description: - Post.title/slug VARCHAR(200), excerpt/cover_image VARCHAR(500), Category/Tag.name VARCHAR(50), Comment.nickname VARCHAR(50), email VARCHAR(100). schemas.py declares plain str. crud create/update catch only IntegrityError. Postgres DataError -> unhandled -> 500 envelope.

ISS-009.title: Over-length write input causes 500 on PostgreSQL (schema/column length mismatch)
ISS-009.description: Users can POST over-length nickname/email/title etc.; SQLite stores it silently, PostgreSQL raises 'value too long for type character varying' -> unchecked DataError -> 500 INTERNAL_ERROR, and the value silently accepted on SQLite means tests never catch it. Validation boundary should reject with 422.

TASK-008.description: Add max_length to schemas.py (Category/Tag name=50, Post title=200, slug=200, excerpt=500, cover_image=500, Comment nickname=50, email=100) and admin NameRequest.name=50. Postgres then rejects over-length input as 422 at validation instead of DataError->500; SQLite/Postgres behavior converges. Tests: 422 for over-length, 201 for boundary length.

DEC-004.title: Accept per-process in-memory caches under multi-worker staleness
DEC-004.rationale: Post list (TTL 300s) and categories/tags (TTL 1800s) caches are process-local TTLCache. docker-compose runs uvicorn --workers 2, so each worker invalidates only its own cache on writes; the other worker serves stale entries bounded by TTL (≤5min posts, ≤30min taxonomies). At this blog's scale the worst-case staleness is cosmetic and self-heals; views/likes never invalidate list cache by design (ordering unchanged).
DEC-004.alternatives_rejected: Redis-backed shared cache (new infra + ops cost, no multi-node deployment yet); single uvicorn worker (loses concurrency for a latent-cosmetic gain); versioned cache keys with a shared clock (still needs Redis to be correct).
